who: Todd E. Robinson, historian of African American and urban history at UNLV, PhD in history from Michigan.

Summer Marie Cherland’s 2014 UNLV history dissertation lists Todd E. Robinson as first committee member.
The February 2015 article identifies UNLV history professor Todd E. Robinson as author of A City Within a City.
LC identifies Todd E. (Todd Ephraim) Robinson through A city within a city (2013).

notes: The student record, Michigan doctorate, full name and book identify the LC candidate.

who: Enrique A. Sanabria, historian of modern Iberia at the University of New Mexico, PhD UC San Diego 2001.

The department states that Enrique A. Sanabria joined UNM in 2002 as a specialist in modern Spain.
LC establishes Enrique A. Sanabria from Republicanism and anticlerical nationalism in Spain (2009).

notes: Exact doctorate institution/year, faculty affiliation, name and monograph agree.

who: James A. Schafer, Jr., historian of American medicine at the University of Houston, PhD Johns Hopkins 2007.

Timothy Vale’s CV names James A. Schafer, Jr. of Houston as chair of his 2022 dissertation, Lone-Star Strong.

who: Glenn Sonnedecker, historian of pharmacy and science at Wisconsin–Madison, PhD Wisconsin 1952.

LC identifies Glenn Sonnedecker through Kremers and Urdang’s History of pharmacy (1963), with earlier heading Glenn Allen Sonnedecker.

who: Loyd S. Swenson, Jr., historian of science and space exploration at the University of Houston, PhD Claremont 1962.

evidence.says: The History of Science Society lists Loyd S. Swenson, Jr. as Houston history professor with a 1962 Claremont Graduate School PhD.

The Houston Chronicle obituary identifies Loyd Sylvan Swenson, Jr. as Houston history professor emeritus, with a Claremont doctorate and a career at Houston; he coauthored histories of the Mercury and Apollo programs.
LC identifies Loyd S. Swenson through This new ocean (1966) and 100 years of science and technology in Texas (1986), recording usage Loyd S. Swenson, Jr.

notes: Name, Jr. usage, doctorate institution/year, Houston career and scholarly field agree.

who: Tracy L. Teslow, historian of science and public history at Cincinnati since 2002, PhD Chicago 2002.

The library record lists Tracy Lang Teslow’s Representing race to the public as a University of Chicago PhD dissertation, 2002.
LC establishes Tracy Teslow, also identified as Tracy L. Teslow, from the prepublication citation Racial science (2014).
The publisher identifies the author of Constructing Race as Cincinnati history professor Tracy Teslow; its cataloging page uses the LC authorized name.

who: John Alden Thayer, historian of modern Italy at Minnesota, PhD Wisconsin in the 1960–61 academic year.

evidence.says: Minnesota’s biennial report lists John Alden Thayer as associate professor of history, with a Wisconsin PhD dated 1961.
The 1979 AHA program lists John Thayer of Minnesota chairing a session on nineteenth-century Italian and French criminology.
Wisconsin lists John Thayer’s dissertation, Italy: The Post Risorgimento and the Great War, under George Mosse in 1960–1961.
LC identifies John Alden Thayer, using John A. Thayer, as author of Italy and the great war (1964), then a Georgetown assistant professor of history.

notes: Minnesota’s full-name record and Wisconsin dissertation connect the supervisor to the LC historian of Italy. Minnesota dates the PhD 1961; AHA lists 1960, within Wisconsin’s 1960–61 academic year.
